title: A busy MP4 lands at the size the Export sheet said
goal: When a screen recording is full of fast-moving detail, like scrolling a page of text, the MP4 that lands can be twice the size the Export sheet quoted, so someone who picked Small to get under a chat limit finds their file does not fit.
notes: Measured 2026-09-25 on an idle machine (the-export-size-test-fails-about-one-run-in-thre), 3 s 1280x800 scrolling-text source (VideoExportBudgetTests.scrollingText is the same picture), bytes landed against recipe.expectedBytes: at 300 px/s High 1,564,796 vs 1,382,400, Standard 1,104,754 vs 921,600, Small 546,480 vs 324,000 (+69%); at 900 px/s High 1,733,042, Standard 1,548,584 (+68%), Small 830,895 vs 324,000 (+156%). RecordingExport.weight shows min(budget, measuredCost) with 'about', so the sheet shows at most the budget. The system H.264 encoder treats AVVideoAverageBitRateKey as a target and overshoots on detail-heavy frames (key frame every 2 s). Tried adding kVTCompressionPropertyKey_DataRateLimits [bitrate/8 bytes, 1 s] via AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey: Small at 900 px/s came to 490,901 (still +52%) and High at 300 px/s fell to 979,188 (-29%, under), so a hard limit alone is not the answer; a second-pass or a quality-based (not bitrate-based) estimate may be. The software encoder (EnableHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder false) overshoots far worse: Small 1,256,251. Pure noise overshoots ~10x at every choice but is not screen material. Under concurrent encodes the sizes also swing wildly (Standard 1.1 to 3.1 MB), which nothing in the app can control.
acceptance: On a 3 second 1280x800 recording of text scrolling at 300 and at 900 pixels a second, each of High, Standard and Small lands within 25 per cent of the size the sheet shows for it
The same holds on the easy recordings the export tests already use, so an easy recording is not pushed far under its number
If the encoder cannot be held to the number, the sheet shows a number that the file really lands near, and a test says which
